title.narrative: Emergency WASH Lifesaving support to contested areas of Ofla, Korem town, Zata and Chercher

description.narrative: ltpgtAn emergency WASH project planned in the project will address critical needs of community residing in Zata, Ofla, Korem and Cherecher Woredas. The proposed emergency WASH assistance project is designed in line with the Humanitarian Response Plan Strategic Objectives, and third round reserve allocation of EHF 2024. The proposed response focus on most vulnerable community that are highly affected by the Northern conflict and drought. Zata, Ofla, Korem and Cherecher are contested areas where the two border regions, arenbsprecurrently competing for territorial issues. The community has faced repeated conflict including displacement. As the areas are receiving insufficient rainfall, drought is another common problem repeatedly affecting the area where food insecurity is a prevalent problem.nbsp As a result, the target woredas are designated for funding in the EHF third round reserve allocation. ltbrgtThe proposed project intervention consisting of WASH responses is desire to contribute for the achievement of strategic objectives 1 3 of HRP strategic objectives focuses on a three-pronged approach. ltbrgtDue to a strong presence in the zone, the Norwegian Church Aid (NCA) is well-positioned to collaborate and respond to the challenges faced by vulnerable households affected by drought, displacement, and limited access to necessities. This collaborative effort will work closely with key government sectors to prevent further deterioration of emergency water and sanitation and contributing for improvement of health and nutrition for affected communities in the proposed locations.ltbrgtNCA will manage the project, including baseline and endline surveys, partner capacity building, monitoring, procurement, transportation and distribution of WASH NFI, rehabilitation of nonfunctional water schemes and sanitation facilities, coordination platforms, quality and CHS compliance, and reporting. NCA will jointly implement activities at the ground level, working with the community and local officials.ltbrgtThe 12-month project with a budget of $600,000 will focus on WASH (100%)). Activities include Improve access to safe water supply systems through rehabilitation of non-functioning water supply systems and/or pipeline extensions strengthen community capacity for management of water points and promote water conservation to improve the functionality of water points,nbsp Improve access to improved sanitation facilities by maintenance and rehabilitation of latrines and sanitation facilities,nbsp Promote improved hygiene practices through dissemination of key hygiene and sanitation messages and distribution of basic hygiene kits (NFIs). Improve access to clean water and sanitation facilities in healthcare facilities for the prevention of cholera, acute watery diarrhoea, and waterborne outbreaks related to poor hygiene conditions.ltbrgtMonitoring and evaluation will be conducted through field observation, Post distribution monitoring, KAP survey, beneficiary feedback, and stakeholder visits. The project aims to improve access to safe water and sanitation and contribute for reduction of malnutrition and disease prevalence. The proposed project is targeting 30,000 individuals mainly IDPs/returnees and vulnerable host communities residing in the four proposed locations. The project will prioritize vulnerable groups like pregnant/lactating women, children, elderly, peoples with disability, IDPs, and food insecure households in host communities.ltbrgtlt/pgt
